speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through catching up on supply and managing demand, we are stabilising the housing market and there are signs that this is happening.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And prior to 2019, HDB launched about 16,000 to 17,000 new flats per year, a figure that Mr Louis Chua had also noted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But at that time, the WP thought that was too many and said so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Now, we have 20,000 flats per year and it seems the WP thinks it is too few.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, I have to ask what figure does the WP propose?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And should your higher number be adopted and if the market comes down due to over-supply, then, what will your party be saying then?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I notice that Mr Louis Chua appeared to express some puzzlement about where all this demand for housing is coming from and he seems to want to link this to population increase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In fact, Mr Louis Chua should know because we have brought this up, we have mentioned this during the debate on the housing Motion in February this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have been building HDB flats faster than the HDB population growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And, in fact, the average number of persons constituting each HDB household has been going down.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is the decrease in household size that Mr Louis Chua has also noted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And what is the cause of this reduction in household size?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One factor, and I think this is a long-term one, has to do with the fact that we have heard the housing aspirations of singles and we have, over the years, progressively provided more housing options for the singles so that there are more housing types that they can buy, be it on the resale or the BTO market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And, in fact, we have further open this up with the new BTO classification framework that was announced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Given rising rates of singlehood, even if the population were to remain completely static, demand for housing is going to increase over time because the reduction of household sizes is set to continue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is the reason why I seek Mr Louis Chua and the WP support for all our levers on both the demand as well as on the supply side.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Please support us in having a robust recycling strategy for our land in addition to having careful land planning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These are familiar points because he has also raised them during the debate in February.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He talked about the PSP's proposal of an "Affordable Housing Scheme".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And as far as I can make out, the affordable housing scheme tries to do a few things.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It seeks to achieve dramatically lower BTO prices by leaving out land cost at the point of first purchase, while seeking to assure existing homeowners that their home values will not be destroyed via a crash in the resale market and avoiding being seen as raiding the Reserves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, the first aim is simply incompatible with the second and the third aims, which is why the proposal was met with considerable scepticism, from Members of this House as well as the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More importantly, the affordable housing scheme does not address the specific imbalances in the housing market that the Government has already responded to and identified.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, dramatically lowering BTO prices is likely to trigger even more demand, especially in the very popular prime areas, instead of moderating demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On the other hand, the Plus/Prime model which we have announced will address this concern.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I now turn to Mr Leong Mun Wai's mention of his Millennial Apartments scheme and I would also like to address some points that Mr Louis Chua has made about addressing the rental market in flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I say this to Mr Leong Mun Wai and Mr Louis Chua.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Let us listen to what younger Singaporeans want.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MND and HDB have been engaging Singaporeans at large but also younger home buyers or prospective home buyers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And most of the younger Singaporeans we have engaged indicated a preference to own their own homes; own rather than rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, we are not closed to new ideas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have, indeed, been hearing inputs from Singaporeans about alternative typologies of housing but we also have to recognise that the very strong desire for home ownership is present within Singaporeans and we will have to prioritise building for home ownership, not so much building for rent, especially if we are talking about people of middle-income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Allow me to move onto concerns raised by several Members, including Mr Leong Mun Wai, Ms He Ting Ru, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Mr Xie Yao Quan on food, especially cooked food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We had proactively launched the Budget Meal initiative in 2023 to increase the availability of affordable food options in HDB estates, especially for residents who need them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These budget meal options are typically lunch or dinner meal options that are priced affordably and are comparable to meals sold at lower price points at nearby eateries, including HDB coffee shops or hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have observed that rental coffeeshops leased under the Price-Quality Method (PQM) tenders typically provide budget food options with prices at around $3 to $3.50, across different estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I should add at this point that operator proposals for PQM tenders that include healthier food options are already given more points and more favourably considered under the quality criteria.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, I want to thank Ms He Ting Ru for supporting this idea.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members of public can use the BudgetMealGoWhere site to find out what budget meals are offered at HDB coffeeshops near them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB also puts up decals at participating coffeeshops to help residents identify the participating stalls more easily.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, while we help residents with their cost of food, we are also mindful that rising costs affect everyone, including coffeeshop operators and stallholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the spirit of partnering Singaporeans under Forward Singapore, we soft-launched an effort last month to crowdsource the public's recommendations and verification of budget meals in coffee shops across the island.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Using the CrowdTaskSG portal, the public can be part of this nation-wide pilot campaign called the Great Budget Meal Hunt by submitting information on affordable meals they would recommend to others or by verifying the details of a budget meal listed on the BudgetMealGoWhere site.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the past week and a half, we have received 245 recommendations of affordable meals and 319 verifications across 91 coffee shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We welcome Singaporeans to contribute actively to this initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While the current budget meal initiative only applies to coffee shops rented out by HDB, there are also sold eating houses that are privately owned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB is studying regulatory options to require budget meals to be provided in these sold eating houses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This includes making the provision of budget meals a condition for the renewal of use of the outdoor refreshment areas – an idea that Mr Murali Pillai had raised previously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to work with coffee shop operators to find sustainable ways to offer affordable food options to residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some Members have also raised their concerns that businesses may take advantage of the inflationary environment to raise prices exorbitantly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government takes a strong stance against profiteering and will not hesitate to take action if there is a case to be made.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If Mr Leong has concerns about GST misrepresentation, in other words, a business unjustifiably raising prices by attributing it to GST increase, he can make a submission too to the CAP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, there is also broad recognition also that many businesses are facing rising costs, as Mr Mark Lee has pointed out, including the cost of utilities, manpower, rental and raw materials, and some may need to raise prices in order to remain viable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The best safeguard against profiteering is healthy competition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have a robust system in place to remove impediments to competition and encourage a diversified supply chain, which help to ensure that businesses compete fairly and that consumers have sufficient choices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government keeps a close watch on the prices of essential goods and services, especially during this challenging period, and will not hesitate to investigate anti-competitive behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Should a member of the public come across such egregious cases, they can report this to the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) and the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If Ms Hazel Poa, as she said in her speech, felt that the scope of the CAP that she sits on is not sufficient for possible upstream cases of price rises to be investigated, I think CCCS would be glad to hear from her with regards to specific details and investigate them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To further help Singaporeans make better purchase decisions on essentials, CASE has developed an app Price Kaki to compare the prices of items sold at supermarkets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To address potential concerns about shrinkflation, CASE has introduced a unit pricing feature this year on Price Kaki to help consumers more easily compare the prices of products with different package sizes and across different brands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Specifically, on business rentals, Ms Hazel Poa had suggested releasing guidelines on fair rental prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is to ensure industry-wide consistency in leasing principles and practices to provide certainty to landlords and tenants and set out a dispute resolution process that is affordable and expedient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The code will be reviewed and updated as necessary, based on feedback from industry players.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We empathise with the challenges of those who need additional support, such as caregivers and persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To Mr Dennis Tan's points, I would like to clarify that financial support schemes for caregivers such as the Home Caregiving Grant or the Migrant Domestic Worker Levy Concession do not just apply to caregivers of disabled seniors but persons with disabilities too, including care recipients with autism spectrum disorder or intellectual disability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Similarly, all Singapore residents have basic health insurance coverage for life, regardless of pre-existing health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MSF has also recently increased funding to adult disability homes and day activity centres in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, cost of living is an issue that touches the lives of all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have experienced high inflation for the last few years due to the dislocations in the global economy caused by the pandemic, conflict and geopolitical tensions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We try our best to operate public services efficiently and to keep costs low.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, cost is inevitable as things still cost money.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When costs go up, despite our best efforts, they still have to be covered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For essentials, some of it will be covered by Government subsidies, for example, healthcare and public transport costs, but not all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some part needs to be paid by consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will provide them targeted direct help if need be, for example, U-Save rebates and public transport vouchers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And those who need more help will get more support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is much better than subsidising the product directly or having tiered pricing schemes because that is more expensive and less effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Overall, we have provided high quality Government and public services to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government Budget is less than 20% of the GDP, which is much lower than most developed countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Nevertheless, the Government's spending needs are rising steadily, especially in healthcare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is no good time to do it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But through the Assurance Package, the Government has effectively delayed the impact on most citizen households while getting the new rate implemented and the additional revenues flowing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, the bulk of the GST revenues are paid by higher-income groups as well as foreigners and tourists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While the Government is helping most Singaporean households, the higher-income groups as well as foreigners will contribute more to Government revenue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through this combination of not delaying necessary adjustments while providing needed support to households, we can keep our public services and finances sound while helping Singaporeans going through a difficult time (In English): I would like to take this opportunity to highlight the point that was just raised – I believe it was by Mr Louis Chua – on delaying GST increase for one or two years on the basis that finances have been better than expected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are actually doing much better than that.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many are cutting back on spending while we ride out the economic uncertainties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We empathise with these challenges and we will do more, if necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This means: one. preserving market principles and not over-regulating – to allow the market to allocate resources and determine price so that we can have an efficient, productive economy while intervening decisively where market failures exist; and two, fiscal sustainability – to intervene prudently so as to remain responsible to future generations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the longer term, the only bulwark against inflation is to remain competitive, to grow the economy and to achieve wage growth for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is the sustainable and sensible way ahead and this Government is committed to this mission.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: But before that, I do need to highlight that I think all of us agree here that policy-making needs to be dynamic.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: As what the Leader of the Opposition, Mr Pritam Singh, has said in his opening speech, we need to ensure that our policies are reflective of the circumstances today and tomorrow versus the past.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: In this regard, I also acknowledge and agree with the Senior Minister of State when she shared that the reduction in household sizes is a key factor in driving housing demand.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I also note that just in the last five years, you see that the average household size has come down very rapidly from about 3.5 to close to about three.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I agree that even if the population remains static, that is going to be a significant source of demand, but the population is not static.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: At the same time, the uncertainty I was expressing is that if you look at the population growth rate today, that appears to be a step up, not just in percentage.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I think this is also a big question mark – as to what then is the forward looking policy when it comes to the incoming net migration, because as far as I understand, our total fertility rate (TFR) is at an all-time low.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I think a lot of the new housing demand is also driven by the population policies.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: At the same time, as I shared in my speech, we are looking at a record high number of marriages.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I think that was recently reported in the last one to two months.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: That appears, again, to be a step up in the housing demand versus what we have seen in the past decade or so.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: All these factors, put together, would suggest that perhaps, if we look at housing demand, that appears to have stepped up versus what it was previously.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I agree with what the Senior Minister of State has shared earlier.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: So, the clarification – two clarifications here —

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: Sorry, the two clarifications here is that I understand that the Government has ramped up the supply of BTO flats, but I am still not sure as to why when it comes to rental flats, there is a significant reduction in the pace of increase.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This will continue and we seek to get back on track.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Not only do we seek to get back on track, we do recognise the need to have a buffer.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is also something that Members have talked about.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It is something that we do agree with.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is also the reason why we are seeking to ramp up supply of Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS) flats.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We know that this is very important to Singaporeans who are waiting for key collection.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In terms of population growth, we have discussed population growth in this House over the years.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I do not propose to go over it in detail.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Suffice to say, we have seen that in the last few years, due to COVID-19, that has caused very sharp fluctuations in population.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I believe that the sharpest growth post-COVID-19 and the reopening of our economy in terms of non-citizens actually would be the category would not be living in our HDB flats, particularly, the migrant workers.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But overall the Government is planning to ensure that through our land use planning as well as making sure that we have got all the supply side and demand side factors in place to ensure a steady supply, both of private as well as public housing.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And I thank Mr Louis Chua for also agreeing on the observations that I have made.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I made these remarks yesterday, but I notice that today there are more Members who are in this House.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am going to repeat my remarks that I made yesterday.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Which is that in the past, Members have taken this opportunity for raising points of clarification to make mini speeches before asking their clarification.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As I highlighted yesterday, there have been occasions where one such mini speech exceeded five minutes.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I want to remind Members that under Standing Order 48(3), no Member other than the mover – and in this case, it is Mr Pritam Singh – is allowed to speak more than once on a Motion.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Making a point of clarification or asking supplementary questions are not the occasions for a second speech.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will certainly allow some leeway for Members to explain their point of clarification or make your question intelligible, but I ask Members please, for your cooperation and understanding, to observe the Standing Orders and to keep your points of clarification and questions concise and to the point.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I have two clarifications for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And two, when the Plus and Prime flats come into operations, will this deficit actually go up higher?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: That is why much as we would like to be as generous as we can, we also need to be responsible.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We need to be good stewards of public resources and we have to run the public housing building programme with sustainability in mind.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As to whether or not with the Prime and Plus going forward whether there will be more subsidies, I think that is not something that we can determine just simply by the introduction of the framework alone.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But the intention of the framework is to streamline demand, streamline demands so that people would make quite prudent choices and it will emphasise the principle of owner occupation and what I can say to Mr Leong is that the subsidies will be very well used.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: I just wanted to make a quick clarification that in my speech, I was asking for more consideration and weightage to be given to outlets and restaurants that actually offer healthier options.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: I was not saying that it was not already being done. but I think the point is well taken.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I think on the principle we are not disagreeing and I happened to share Ms He Ting Ru's passion for healthy food so this is certainly something that we will look into.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But we also have to balance against the other relevant considerations for quality because after all, coffee shops do serve a wider range of consumers and residents.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And people have different preferences for what they want to see in the coffee shop.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, comparing with our Affordable Home Scheme — of course, there will be issues that we still need to discuss about the Affordable Home Scheme.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But the current Government home scheme, do you agree that it has led to high HDB prices?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: At the same time, every BTO flat, not only the buyers pay for the land cost but all Singaporeans have to pay for the deficit?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I am afraid the nature of Mr Leong's question is not very clear.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Could Mr Leong rephrase his question, Mr Speaker?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: What I mean is that I am trying to compare our Affordable Home Scheme with the current BTO scheme of the Government.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Of course, there will be some disadvantages, some problems, some issues that we need to overcome, but I think the Affordable Home Scheme's problems can be overcome too.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, we are making a policy decision here.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The current BTO scheme has led to increasing prices of the BTO, because you have to incorporate the rising land cost.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: As a result, it has led to rising HDB prices.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, there are two disadvantages of the current BTO scheme.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I am afraid I will have to answer Mr Leong's question with a question of my own.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: He has not made clear how his Affordable Housing Scheme does not result in the outcome that he claims the BTO scheme has created?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It seeks to dramatically lower BTO prices by leaving out land costs at the point of first purchase.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But perhaps his party is worried that the scheme will be rejected outright by homeowners who are worried about a crash in the resale price so it tries to assure people that it does not do.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If I may, actually this topic was subject to a debate in a previous Sitting for which we came to a conclusion.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Let us come back to the Motion at hand and let us confine our clarifications to the speeches relating to the Motion proposed by Mr Pritam Singh.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am just saying that based on what the Senior Minister of State has said, does she agree that the current schemes has got these two disadvantages: one, HDB prices will continue to go up as long as land cost goes up; two, and when the Government or HDB sells the BTO flat, there will be a subsidy and this translate into HDB deficit and this deficit goes to the budget and all Singaporeans have to pay for it?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: We should not be wasting time on revisiting this debate over and over again.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: So, can I ask Mr Speaker to make a —

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: So, can I invite Mr Speaker to make a decision on this so that we can move out of this debate.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Otherwise, we will be going back to issues which we have debated over and over again, and now resurfacing yet again.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I thought Mr Leong was going to make a different point of clarification.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will allow one last response if Minister of State Sim Ann wants to make it; and then I am going to move on.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, it seems to me that Mr Leong is tying himself up in knots and I am not convinced that members of the public will agree that static prices over the long term is what the housing policy should be aiming for.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: If you want to subsidise any product, be it housing, be it education for that matter, defence, street lighting, these are public goods that are provided.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, I really think that for both Mr Leong's good and for the House's good, I think we should pasue this because Mr Leong, you are leading yourself down a path of no return.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can I invite Mr Pritam Singh to make your closing?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: We have no substantive quarrel with Amendment No 3, which does not substantially change the thrust of our Motion.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Amendment No 1 which states that "cost of living is a global concern" reads as an attempt to minify the role Government can and should play to reduce cost of living burdens on Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: While global factors are important, these should instead prompt a review of existing policies with the view to relieve cost of living pressures.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: We also disagree with Amendment No 2 and its use of the words "continue pursuing policies".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The use of the word "continue" suggests to us, at least, that the status quo is fine.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Indeed, we have proposed specific structural changes to the system that we believe will work better than current policies.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On the electricity front, Member of Parliament for Aljunied GRC, Ms Sylvia Lim observed that the need for Singaporeans to conserve energy is more urgent than ever, given the risks of high prices and supply shortages caused by conflicts around the world.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: She recounted the Government's answer to managing household electricity bills, was the open electricity market.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But the dramatic failures of retailers in 2021 has cast doubt on the viability of the open energy market to bring down household electricity bills.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: She asked the Government to look again at her earlier suggestion of tiered electricity pricing and to also consider lowering charges for consumption during off-peak hours.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Staying on utilities and specifically water prices, my contribution to this debate was my calling on the Government to review the price structure of water for both domestic and non-domestic consumers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Such a review would have the objective of creating a more fairly tiered structure that promotes water conservation and potentially lowest cost for business and many households.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Aljunied GRC Member of Parliament, Mr Faisal Manap, reiterated the call he made in 2014 to the Government to establish a means of assessing the effectiveness of our social safety net.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Back then, he proposed that Singapore adopt the International Labour Organization (ILO)'s social protection framework.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: He suggested that if the Government prefers a more localised framework, the Government should then look at the minimum income standard published for households in Singapore, reports that have been published by local academics led by Assoc Prof Teo You Yenn and Dr Ng Kok Hoe.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Government is not precluded from publishing its own list of basic needs and those extras required for thriving in Singapore as a way of tracking outcomes for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Sengkang GRC Member of Parliament, Ms He Ting Ru's speech covered several keynotes in health and the health and care ecosystem where the Government can and should be working harder to control the cost of healthy living in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Her speech reflects the WP's concern about the effect by increasing cost of care is having on the physical and mental well-being of families and calls for more support in areas like mental healthcare and intermediate and long-term care.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: For instance, she called for MediSave annual limits to be increased in line with medical inflation.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Hougang SMC Member of Parliament, Mr Dennis Tan asked for the current means testing in healthcare to be improved upon to better account for an individual's financial situation and health conditions so that healthcare can be more affordable and accessible.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: He called for help to be given to more Singaporeans who may need more assistance, even though they may be adjudged not to be eligible based on present household income or annual value of their home, especially when they are not able to receive financial assistance from members of the same household.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: He called for more help to be extended to adults with special needs or other forms of disability who are in the working adult age group, but who are unable to work and require part-time or full-time care from family members, especially in families where the parents are getting on in age.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: More help should also be extended to family members responsible for their caregiving.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On housing, he called for the Government to increase the supply of HDB flats across the for purchase market and also the neglected for rent market, especially as our population growth and housing demand appears to have stepped up.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: To ensure all Singaporeans can access appropriate housing and shelter, addressing the fundamental demand-supply problem would necessitate adjustments to the supply side of the equation so that the market can find the appropriate equilibrium.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: He stressed the importance of smoothing out the vehicle quota supply across the years and seizing the practice of reimbursing early deregistered COEs at their book value.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: He also suggested prohibiting dealers from bidding directly for COEs and treating private hire cars in the same manner as taxis are, which is to have them bid in the open category albeit paying Cat A or Cat B prices.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: This will allow the early profits of the current public transport operators to be redirected to benefit commuters by mitigating fair increases and providing free transport for the elderly and people with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: He explained how the NTC could bring about significant productivity gains and economies of scale when compared to the current public transport model.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The question is how would this reduction in price come about?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Would it be from the Chief Valuer relooking at how land is priced for public housing, or as should be assumed, from an increase in taxpayer subsidies from HDB flats, drawn from the yearly Budget?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Inevitably, it is a taxpayer that is going to foot the bill for a larger HDB subsidy to make HDB flats cheaper.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And this is an amount that the Government believes it can absorb without an increase in taxes.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Otherwise, it would not have pursued the new HDB BTO classification system.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In the same spirit, Mr Speaker, the WP believes that we should continue to look beyond short-term relief in addressing this cost of living crisis and to relook at prevailing orthodoxies on other schemes so as to lower cost for Singaporeans and their families.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: A few other proposals will put cash in the hands of vulnerable workers and seniors to help them navigate their way out of this difficult period, for example, by reviewing with a fresh perspective, both MediSave, as well as the Workfare Income Supplement.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: A few other proposals may prompt behavioural shifts towards greater efforts to reduce wastage and more sensitivity to sustainable usage of utilities, such as water and electricity.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: At their core, all the proposals prompt the Government to relook at its legacy policy with an eye on battling the cost of living crisis that Singaporeans find themselves deeply mired in.
